channel.title: Muhammad Jahanzaib Awan — Writing
channel.description: Short technical posts on machine learning, evaluation and data science.

item.title: Curriculum Learning: Ordering Training Data on Purpose
item.description: Most training pipelines shuffle data and hope. Curriculum learning asks what happens if you don't, and the answer is more nuanced than 'easy first, hard later'.

item.title: Explaining a Model's Decision When Nobody Trusts the p-value
item.description: When a p-value fails to persuade, swap it for concrete numbers on money, customers, and risk. Here is how I do that in practice.

item.title: Data Contracts for ML Pipelines: Catching Schema Drift Early
item.description: Schema drift breaks models silently. Data contracts catch it at the source, before it poisons training data or corrupts predictions in production.

item.title: Multi-Modal Models Explained: Fusing Text and Image
item.description: A grounded look at how text and image models actually get fused, without the hand-waving about 'understanding'.

item.title: Batch Size: The Quiet Hyperparameter Nobody Tunes
item.description: Batch size is treated as a memory afterthought, but it changes gradient noise, generalisation, and wall-clock time in ways learning rate alone cannot fix.

item.title: Feature Engineering for Tabular Data: What Still Wins
item.description: On tabular data, careful feature engineering often beats a neural network. Here is the intuition, a worked example, and why leakage-aware evaluation matters more than architecture.

item.title: Zero-Shot Classification: Promise Versus Practice
item.description: Zero-shot classification is genuinely useful, but its accuracy claims often collapse once you check for label leakage, prompt sensitivity, and domain mismatch.

item.title: Exploration Versus Exploitation, Without the Slot Machine
item.description: Skip the casino metaphor. Here is the exploration versus exploitation tradeoff explained through a decision you have actually made.

item.title: Synthetic Data for Vision: Closing the Domain Gap
item.description: Synthetic data can rescue a vision project starved of labels, but only when the gap between rendered and real pixels is measured, not assumed away.

item.title: Active Learning: Choosing What to Label Next
item.description: Instead of labelling everything, active learning picks the examples most likely to improve your model, saving budget without sacrificing performance.

item.title: Evaluating Recommenders: Accuracy Is the Wrong First Metric
item.description: A recommender can top the accuracy leaderboard and still be useless. Here is why offline accuracy metrics need company, not replacement.

item.title: Class Imbalance Beyond Binary: Skewed Multi-Class Problems
item.description: Binary imbalance tricks do not simply generalise to multi-class problems. Here is how to think about skewed classes properly, with a worked example.

item.title: Data Leakage in Time Series: Lag Features Need Care
item.description: Lag features feel safe because they look backwards, but sloppy construction lets future information leak in and inflates your validation scores.

item.title: Hyperparameter Search: Grid, Random, and Bayesian, Honestly
item.description: Grid search is comfortable, random search is underrated, and Bayesian optimisation earns its complexity only sometimes. Here is the honest comparison.

item.title: Explaining Transformers Without the Film Analogy Trap
item.description: Skip the film analogies. Here is how to explain transformers to non-technical people using a concrete weighted-vote example that actually holds up.

item.title: What a Model Evaluation Framework Automates and Assumes
item.description: Evaluation frameworks automate splitting, scoring, and aggregation, but they quietly assume your data is independent, your split reflects deployment, and your metric means what you think.

item.title: How to Shortlist MLOps Tools Without Chasing Every Release
item.description: A practical filter for choosing MLOps tools on a small team, so you stop re-evaluating your stack every time something new trends.

item.title: Data Science Salary Bands Explained by Skill
item.description: Salary bands in data science track judgement under uncertainty, not tool familiarity. Here is the skill ladder that actually explains the pay gap.

item.title: Building a Personal MLOps Toolkit Before Paying for a Platform
item.description: Managed MLOps platforms solve real problems, but most of those problems can be handled first with free tools, discipline, and a bit of scripting.

item.title: Why Extreme Risk Evaluation Needs More Than a Test Set
item.description: Held-out accuracy answers a narrow question. For rare, high-consequence failures, you need adversarial probing, distribution shift tests, and honest uncertainty, not just a leaderboard score.
